Juran Chandra Mondal
Vs.
Rabindra Nath Mondal
full_judgment:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarkar, J. This Rule at the instance of the plaintiffs is directed against the judgment and order dated 29-12-83 passed by the Munsif Upazills Kotwali para, Faridpur in Misc. case No.37 of 1983 allowing an application under order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. setting aside the exparte decree dated 9-3-83. 

 2. The petitioners have filed Title suit No. 115 of 1974 in the Court of Munsif Gopalganj against the opposite party and others for a declaration of their title and confirmation of possession in respect of the suit land and the said suit was decreed exparte of 9-3-82. Thereafter the opposite party who was defendant No.3 in the suit filed on application under order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. which was registered as Misc. case no.37 of 1983 for seating aside the exparte decree on the ground inter alia that no summons or registered letter was served upon him and that the services return has been shown as duly served in collusion with the process server. The opposite party came to know about the exparte decree on 30-3-83 when petitioner No.1 disclosed about the exparte decree. Thereafter the opposite party made a search in the court and got information about the date of his knowledge. 

 4. Mr. Shahid Alam, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the rule contends that the learned Munsif compared the signature of the opposite party in the service return with his, signatures take in the courts and found that both the signatures tally. The learned Munsif also observed that the opposite party and defendant No. 4 reside in the same homestead and as such the opposite party should have knowledge about the exparte-decree earlier than the date mentioned by him. Yet the learned Munsif allowed the Misc. case being of the opinion that the opposite party should get a chance to contest the original suit to prove his title to the suit land. According to Mr. Alam, the learned Munsif virtually found that summons was duly served upon the opposite party and as such the learned Munsif erred in law in allowing an application under order 9. Rule 13 C.P.C. and setting aside the exparte decree. Mr. Bazlur Rahman Talukdar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party, on the other hand submits that the opposite party as P.W. 1 stated that he had no knowledge of the original suit and that no summons was served upon him. He has also examined as P.W. 2 Dhirendra Nath Barrio who has stated that he did not sign the alleged service return. On the other hand, the plaintiff opposite party adduced no evidence to prove that summons was duly served upon the opposite party. According to Mr. Talukdar the learned Munsif should have found on the evidence on record that no summons was served upon the opposite party. This being a case of non-service of summons the learned Munsif was justified in setting aside the exparte decree. In support of his contention Mr. Talukdar has referred to the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Md. Abdur Rashid and another V. Abdul Barik and another reported in 1984 B.L.D). (A.D.) 83. 

 5. It appears that although the learned Munsif compared the signature in the service return with the signature of P.W. 1 taken in the court he has not come to a definite finding that there was service of summons. On the other hand P.W. 1 stated that there was no service of summons upon him and that he had no knowledge of the original suit prior to the date of his knowledge as given in his application under order 9. Rule 13 C.P.C. P.W. 2 Dhirerndra Nath Barui has also stated that he did not sing the service return Ext.1 as witness. As regards the evidence adduced on behalf of the plaintiffs opposite parties, the learned Munsif found "The O.P. did not take any step to prove the service retain by adducing any evidence. O.P.1 as O.P.W. 1 has told that the process server of Ext.1 is dead. He could bring any other process server who knows the handwriting of Abdus Sattar who served the summons Ext. 1" Thus It appears that the plaintiffs opposite parties failed to prove by adducing cogent evidence that summons of the original suit was served upon opposite party defendant No.3. In that view of the matter, the irresistible conclusion is that there was no service of summons upon defendant No.3 and as such the exparte decree is liable to be set aside. In view of the decision of the Appellate Division referred to above that under order 9. Rule 13 C.P.C. if summons is not Duly served on the defendants that in a good ground for setting aside the exparte decree because service of summons is an essential condition which must be satisfied before the court can proceed to an exparte decree and when a party satisfies the court that summons were not duly served upon him the Court is bound to set aside the exparte decree. In such a case the question of knowledge is not at all relevant and the expert decree will be set aside even if the defendant had knowledge of the institution of the suit. In view of the finding that there was no service of summons the contention of Mr. Shahid Alam that the learned Munsif was wrong in allowing the application on compassionate ground to give a chance to the defendant to contest the suit need not be considered. In that view of the matter, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.
